topic: Offtake and gas-supply momentum 2025-2026 under Glenfarne
wiki_text: After Glenfarne became lead developer (75% of the project JV, named '8 Star Alaska LLC'; State of Alaska/AGDC 25%) in March 2025, the ~20 mtpa Nikiski export project accumulated preliminary offtake/cooperation agreements totaling roughly 13 mtpa, including Japan's JERA and Tokyo Gas and Thailand's PTT (2 mtpa over 20 years); POSCO International signed an agreement covering LNG offtake and steel supply. Per March 2026 statements from CEO Brendan Duval, Alaska LNG still needs ~3 mtpa of additional offtake to reach FID. On the supply side, Glenfarne announced (Jan 2026) precedent agreements with ExxonMobil, Hilcorp Alaska, and Great Bear Pantheon/Pantheon Resources, plus in-state anchors (ENSTAR 30-yr LOI; Donlin Gold up to 50 MMcf/d). Phase One = a 739-mi, 42-in mainline (target mechanical completion 2028, first gas 2029); Phase Two adds the 20 mtpa liquefaction terminal at Nikiski. Project cost cited ~$44B (GEM unit note cites $38.7B for terminal+pipeline).

On 15 May 2026, Longboard TerminalCo (a wholly-owned subsidiary of JERA Americas) requested to begin the FERC pre-filing review for an LNG import terminal in state waters offshore Kalaeloa (Barbers Point), with onshore facilities in Campbell Industrial Park, Oahu. The project would use a disconnectable, non-jurisdictional FSRU (storage ~138,000-174,000 m3) to displace fuel oil; anticipated demand peaks ~1 mtpa (~0.6 mtpa power generation/gas distribution + ~0.4 mtpa marine bunkering). Indicative schedule: formal FERC application by Dec 2026, FERC order by Q2 2028, construction from Q3 2028, online Q1 2030. JERA is a 50-50 JV of TEPCO Fuel & Power (Tokyo Electric) and Chubu Electric.

topic: Cook Inlet LNG FSRU import project detail
wiki_text: Cook Inlet LNG, a unit of Louisiana-based Gardes Holdings, partnering with long-time Cook Inlet producer Glacier Oil & Gas Corp, plans to moor an FSRU alongside the existing Osprey platform on the west side of Cook Inlet as a bridge import supply for southcentral Alaska. Initial structure ~22 Bcf/yr of regas (~0.46 mtpa); LNG tankers ~every 30-45 days in winter; FSRU mooring anchors are the only new infrastructure. First available gas targeted mid-2029; FERC approval process initiated.

Harvest Midstream (via affiliate Harvest Alaska; owned by Jeff Hildebrand, who also owns Hilcorp) closed its acquisition of the long-idled Kenai LNG terminal from Marathon Petroleum in November 2025, repurposing the former export plant as an LNG import/regasification terminal to address a looming southcentral Alaska gas shortfall (Chugach Electric's Hilcorp supply contract expires 31 Mar 2028). Harvest targets FID in Q2 2026 and first LNG imports in H1 2028, and filed with FERC to amend/expand its previously approved Kenai cool-down project to add import capacity.

ST LNG LLC (CEO Sharad Tak / Tak Investments; president Alap Shah, ex-New Fortress FLNG) filed a Deepwater Port license application with MARAD in June 2025 for a fixed-platform-plus-floating LNG export terminal ~10.4 nm off Matagorda, Texas (Brazos OCS Lease Block BA-476). Full build = four 2.1 mtpa liquefaction systems (8.4 mtpa total) using four converted LNG carriers, with a 5.5-mi 30-in pipeline lateral. ST LNG also sought DOE export authorization; expects MARAD approval by ~June 2026, possible FID as early as Q2 2026, and first LNG loading from Phase 1 in 2029.
